answer: An agent economy can anchor identity to a locked bond. Before voting or trading, each agent posts collateral that peers can verify, and only staked agents count. A sybil attacker who wants a thousand fake voices must fund a thousand separate bonds, so the cost scales linearly with every forged identity, and caught double-dealing slashes the stake. That knoll of at-risk collateral raises the price of mass registration, making fake accounts unprofitable. Requiring this jade standard of real, forfeitable stake stops one actor from multiplying itself into a misleading majority.
